meta.title: AdS from CFT for scalar QED
meta.abstractHtml: We construct an explicit bulk dual in anti-de Sitter space, with couplings of order , for the -singlet sector of QED in space-time dimensions () coupled to scalar fields. We begin from the bulk dual for the theory of complex free scalar fields that we constructed in our previous work, and couple this to gauge fields living on the boundary in order to get the bulk dual of scalar QED (in which the gauge fields become the boundary value of the bulk vector fields). As in our previous work, the bulk dual is non-local but we can write down an explicit action for it. We focus on the CFTs arising at low energies (or, equivalently, when the gauge coupling goes to infinity). For we discuss also the addition of a Chern-Simons term for , modifying the boundary conditions for the bulk gauge field. We also discuss the generalization to QCD, with gauge fields coupled to scalar fields in the fundamental representation (in the large limit with fixed ).

children.body: The AdS/CFT correspondence [1, 2, 3] is an equivalence between theories of quantum gravity on asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) space in dimensions, and conformal quantum field theories (CFTs) in dimensions. Since for we do not have any non-perturbative definition of these quantum gravity theories, the correspondence should be viewed as providing a non-perturbative definition for these theories in terms of the corresponding quantum field theories, whenever those are known and well-understood. In many cases of the correspondence the gravitational theories have a classical limit, in which the ratio of the Planck scale to the radius of anti-de Sitter space goes to infinity, and which corresponds to a large limit of some sort in the CFT side. In those cases one can test the correspondence by checking that the semi-classical expansion on the gravity side agrees with the large limit of the corresponding field theories.

A derivation of the AdS/CFT correspondence requires showing that the CFT can be rewritten as a quantum gravity theory, in the sense that its expansion reproduces the corresponding perturbative expansion around some gravitational solution in AdS space. While one can often test this for specific observables, providing such a derivation for the full theory is challenging (see [4, 5, 6, 7] for some recent progress in relating free symmetric orbifold CFTs to string theory on ). In our recent paper [8] we provided such a derivation for the simplest case of the AdS/CFT correspondence – the duality [9] between the -singlet sector of free complex scalar fields in dimensions, and a theory of higher-spin gravity on . Our derivation in [8] followed the methods of bi-local holography [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15], in its Lorentz-invariant version. We first changed variables in the CFT from the free scalar fields () to their bi-local combinations

(1.1)

which capture all the information about -invariant observables in the theory (at least in flat space). In the large expansion one can write down an action for that reproduces the correlators of the original theory, to all orders in (as discussed in [8], the mapping to the bi-local variables makes sense also for finite but it is more subtle then, and in this paper we only discuss the theory in the expansion). In order to map this to a theory in AdS space, we first expanded the bi-local field in a basis of eigenstates of the Euclidean conformal group . We then showed that the same eigenstates appear in the expansion of transverse traceless fields of spin () living on a fixed space, enabling a one-to-one mapping between these fields and the bi-local (1.1). Using this mapping we rewrote the action of the original theory as an action (with coupling ) for fields in AdS space. This action is explicitly known but is non-local. For a specific choice of the undetermined coefficients appearing in the mapping, the quadratic term in the bulk can be chosen to be local. Since the -singlet sector of free scalars is conjectured [9] to be dual to Vasiliev’s high-spin gravity theory [16, 17, 18], we believe that our action is equivalent to a gauge-fixed version of this theory, in which its fields live on a fixed AdS space-time (as in [19]); the spectrum of physical fields is consistent with this, but the equivalence has not yet been shown.

In this paper, we generalize this construction to the -singlet sector of scalar QED – the theory of a gauge field minimally coupled to charged scalar fields, for . In principle this generalization is straightforward, since on the field theory side it just involves introducing a dynamical gauge field and coupling it to -singlet combinations of the scalar fields, and we can in principle do this also on the gravity side. On-shell, local -invariant operators (such as the ones appearing in the coupling to the gauge field) map to the boundary values of the bulk fields on AdS space; however, the construction above requires the off-shell mapping of the local CFT operators to the bulk, and at first sight this seems to be more complicated. In [8] we showed that for and the naive on-shell mapping works also off-shell, and we used it there to derive the dual to the critical (or ) vector model, by coupling a singlet to the spin operator . In this paper we show that the same is true also for and , and also for higher values of . This allows us to write down a simple action for the -dimensional gauge field coupled to the bulk fields; in fact, as may have been expected [20, 21, 22, 23, 24], the gauge field becomes simply the boundary value of the -dimensional vector field . Thus, compared to the original theory of free scalars, the description of QED just involves changing the boundary condition for the bulk vector field , and perhaps adding some boundary terms for it. The boundary terms are required if one wants to describe QED at finite coupling, but they disappear in the low-energy limit, where QED (for ) flows to a conformal field theory (at least at large and to all orders in [25], and perhaps also for all finite values of [26, 27]). In the special case of one can also add a Chern-Simons coupling at level ; when is kept fixed in the large limit, this coupling is translated into a modified boundary condition for the bulk vector field.

One application of our bulk formalism for QED would be to find classical solutions in the bulk describing monopole operators, and perhaps to use them to compute their correlation functions. As we discuss below, our formalism only includes monopole operators if there is no Chern-Simons coupling for the , and it may be interesting to look for ways to get around this problem so that monopoles in Chern-Simons-matter theories may also be incorporated.

We also generalize our construction to the singlet sector of scalar fields in the fundamental representation of a gauge field (“scalar QCD" [28]), when is kept fixed in the large limit, and for we can again include a Chern-Simons level . The bulk dual is very similar to the QED case, except the bulk fields now transform in the adjoint representation of . Note that this limit is different from the large and fixed limit considered in [29], which is believed to also be dual to a parity breaking higher spin bulk theory. It would be interesting to see if the generalization of our construction to this limit just involves changing boundary conditions, or explicitly changes the bulk interaction terms as a function of (see discussions in [30, 23]). Such a generalization, as well as the inclusion of fermions, would allow us to similarly construct the bulk dual of ABJ theory [31] in its higher spin limit, which could ultimately lead to a connection to string theory and M-theory via the ABJ triality [23, 32].

Finally, our off-shell mapping allows us to construct the bulk dual for the critical or vector model for , as discussed in [33, 34]. This CFT is not unitarity at finite due to complex large instantons [35], but is unitary in the expansion. It would be interesting to study the classical solutions corresponding to these instantons from the bulk perspective using our construction.

We begin in section 2 by describing the -singlet sector of scalar QED in bi-local variables, and translating its action to these variables. In section 3 we review the mapping found in [8] between the free scalar theory and the bulk, and extend it to an off-shell mapping for local operators in the CFT. In section 4 we then use this mapping to construct the bulk dual for the -singlet sector of scalar QED, and show that it reproduces the expansion of this theory. Finally, in section 5 we discuss the generalization to scalar QCD.

children.title: A subtlety in restricting to the singlet sector
children.titleHtml: A subtlety in restricting to the singlet sector

children.body: We will be interested in the singlet sector of scalar QED. In general , we can simply restrict to this sector by hand, which has no nontrivial effects on . For and non-zero , we need to be more careful. What we actually do is first restrict the theory of scalars to its -invariant sector, and then couple this sector to the gauge field. We can perform the restriction in a rigorous way [44] by coupling the theory to a Chern-Simons term at infinite level before coupling to the new gauge field, and we will use this to show that monopole operators cannot appear in the singlet sector (as we define it here) when . Thus, for and non-zero our theory is not precisely the same as the -singlet sector of scalar QED (which could have -singlet monopole operators), but we will still call it by this name. In all other cases our theory includes the full -singlet sector of scalar QED.

Let us start by considering the free theory with action in , with global symmetry . We can gauge this by adding a Chern-Simons term for a gauge field , with scalar couplings:

(2.16)

where is the gauge field, is the current, and in the second line we separated out the terms from the gauge field , which couples to the current defined in (2.2). The gauge-invariant operators are then all singlets of , as we want, but the theory is modified by the extra fields, and in particular it has new monopole operators charged under a topological global symmetry generated by the dual of the field strength of . We can then take the limit, which on removes all dynamical effects of the gauging, including the existence of monopoles charged under the , and we obtain precisely the desired restriction to singlets.

From the -singlet sector of the free theory, we can then get the theory we are interested in (the -singlet sector of scalar QED at level ) by adding , , and as discussed before. For , monopole operators (charged under ) carry units of the gauge charge, and so to be gauge-invariant under the gauging, monopoles needs to be dressed by composites of that will cancel their charge. But then the dressed monopoles would also be charged under the original gauging due to the dressing. Thus, our theory includes no gauge-invariant monopoles for . For , the monopole operators of QED are uncharged under , so they are allowed. Similarly for where we have no Chern-Simons terms, the codimension-3 monopole operators discussed above are also allowed.

In this section, we discuss the exact AdS/CFT map that we will use in the next section to write down the bulk dual of the -singlet sector of scalar QED. We start by reviewing the off-shell AdS/CFT map derived in [8], which naturally acts on the CFT bi-local . We will then show how this map implies that local single-trace operators of any spin in any dimension also map off-shell to the bulk in a simple way, generalizing the and case proven in [8]. For , this off-shell map will then be used to write the bulk dual of scalar QED in the next section.

We begin by briefly reviewing the AdS/CFT map of the free scalar theory [8]. The map is given by expanding the bi-local fluctuation on one side, and the spin transverse traceless AdS fields on the other side, in terms of the same irreducible representations (labeled by ) of the conformal group, so that the exact map between to is given by the convolution of the basis elements in each space.5

children.body: We will now use the AdS/CFT map of the previous section to write the action for the bulk dual of scalar QED. We will first review the bulk action for the free and critical theories, which were derived in [8]. We will then use the off-shell map of single-trace local operators for to show that the bulk QED action is given by a simple deformation of the bulk dual of the free theory. Finally, we will compute correlation functions in the bulk and show that the bulk duals of the free theory and QED only differ by the boundary conditions of the bulk two-point function, as anticipated in [20, 21, 22, 23, 24], where the two-point function is sensitive to the gauge-fixing in the CFT.

children.body: The bulk dual of scalar QED in with scalars that we described in the previous sections can be easily generalized to QCD in with scalars [28], for finite . For we can again consider also the large Chern-Simons level limit with fixed .

We start by considering a free theory of scalars with global symmetry . The singlet sector under the subgroup can be translated to the bulk just like the usual free scalar theory, except that now both the singlet bi-locals in the CFT and their dual bulk fields are adjoints under , and the terms in the bulk action are all single traces of products of matrices. We can then construct the bulk dual of scalar QCD by a procedure similar to the one described in the previous sections: gauging (in the CFT), fixing a gauge convenient for the large expansion, mapping the current (which is a singlet) to the bulk using our usual CFT-to-AdS map, and coupling it to the new gauge fields. The main differences from the Abelian case are that now the Yang-Mills and Chern-Simons terms for contain self-interactions of the gauge fields, and that the gauge-fixing now leads to ghosts (in the adjoint of ) which will live on the boundary and couple to the gauge fields there.

As with QED, the resulting bulk theory is related to the bulk dual of the free theory by a simple change of boundary conditions for the spin one bulk field (in the adjoint of ). Note that this bulk construction is useful for large with fixed , and it does not apply to the limit of large with fixed discussed in [29, 53], which is expected to have a different dual description.

OA is the Samuel Sebba Professorial Chair of Pure and Applied Physics. SMC is supported in part by a Zuckerman STEM leadership fellowship.
